liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Help On The Way** (2 reviews): Listener praises the opening sequence and a slow, funky Franklin's Tower performance; The opening sequence was sharp and strong, less dreamy than later versions [10][15]
- **Franklin's Tower** (2 reviews): Franklin's Tower was new, but the crowd immediately loved the song; The lead in Franklin's Tower brought down the house, short but sweet [12][19]
- **Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): Jerry's lead four minutes into Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad grabbed attention [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1975-09-28.mtx.seamons.102155.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 15 songs; 112 min; rated 4.71/5 by 17 [1]
- **gd1975-09-28.fob.menke-falanga.motb-0069.91770.flac24**: source not stated; 15 songs; 112 min; rated 4.88/5 by 16 [2]
- **gd75-09-28.sbd.bertha-ashley.22257.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 97 min; rated 4.59/5 by 41 [4]. Said about its sound: Sound is excellent, clear, and bright, with a nice open mix, though Phil suffers slightly [15]
- **gd75-09-28.sbd.fink.9392.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 97 min; rated 4.45/5 by 64 [5]. Said about its sound: Sound is excellent, with a faint harmonica audible on some songs despite low mix levels; Sound quality is wonderful, described as strong, raw, warm, and fuzzy [11][18]
- **gd1975-09-28.aud.gofob.86250.flac16**: audience recording; 14 songs; 90 min; rated 4.2/5 by 10 [7]
- **gd1975-09-28.unknown.beggs.236.shnf**: source not stated; 14 songs; 91 min; rated 2.25/5 by 4 [8]

## Around the show

- Jefferson Starship opened the show at this free park performance, which the reviewer ranked top ten [12]
- Jerry broke a string, preventing a transition from Slipknot to Franklin's Tower [17]
- Described as similar to the One from the Vault recording from the same era [11]
- Band seemed unsure of direction, with TLEO sounding like a holiday inn band [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1975-09-28.mtx.seamons.102155.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (SHN & FLAC>AIFF>Final Cut>WAV>FLAC16) [1]. Also: Uploader lists the setlist, including the transition from Truckin' to the Eleven Jam [1]
- **gd1975-09-28.fob.menke-falanga.motb-0069.91770.flac24**: taped by Bob Menke and Louis Falanga; transferred by Bob Menke and Derek McCabe; source: 2 x Sony ECM-270 => Sony TC-152 >> MAC [2]. Also: Dropouts were patched with SBD and mono; King Solomon's Marbles tracked as one song [2]
- **gd75-09-28.sbd.bertha-ashley.22257.sbeok.shnf**: source: Sounboard [4]. Also: Reviewer thanks the person who remastered the show, noting it sounds nice and clean [16]
- **gd75-09-28.sbd.fink.9392.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]
- **gd1975-09-28.aud.gofob.86250.flac16**: transferred by gotfob; source: On Stage Mic's (BY Band) > ? > Dat @ 44.1 [7]. Also: They Love Each Other was missing on the DAT; left channel dropouts patched with right [7]
- **gd1975-09-28.unknown.beggs.236.shnf**: transferred by Brian Beggs; source: ?? > Turtle Tree > CD > SHN [8]. Also: Uploader lists the second set, starting with Beat It On Down The Line [8]
